title: Field names of the P4 session team scope and the P6 notice queue code are not fixed by any source
source: RWB-ITG-E1019-ITG sections 3, 7, 11 and 13; ownership map (GET /me/session owner P4, POST /cases/{caseId}/notices owner P6); Architecture v5 slides 14 and 17
section: 3. Preconditions; 7. Acceptance criteria (AC1, AC5, AC10); 11. Data
description: No source fixes the field names by which the rwb-access session returns the team scope derived from queue membership, or by which the rwb-comms notice response returns the queue and team code it used. The criteria assert those values across two services, so the suite must read them from the published contracts.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-019 defines membershipOf(userId, onDate) returning teamCodes, regionCodes and queueIds as an in-process interface and gives no HTTP shape; the ownership map names GET /me/session and POST /cases/{caseId}/notices without their payloads; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 17 name the paths and the owners only.
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-access and service owner of rwb-comms
proposed: Publish the team scope field in the rwb-access OpenAPI document for GET /me/session and the queue and team code fields in the rwb-comms OpenAPI document for the notice response before the wave 1 exit, or record the field names in the Service Contract Catalog.

title: JOB-03 run surface and exact rerun facade are not specified for an ITG suite
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-03 DailyCaseRun step); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json jobs JOB-03 and api GET /admin/jobs, POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun; RWB-E1-020 sections 12 and 16
description: JOB-03 is a step of DailyCaseRun in rwb-case (slide 44), while the job catalogue read and its rerun are P1 rwb-source-data per the ownership map (x-module P1 in API Specification v4). No source fixes how an ITG suite reads the state of the JOB-03 step of a workflow run on the monitor, what the monitor line of MSG-P1-001 is attached to when the step is a workflow step, whether a rerun of a workflow step is offered through the catalogue, or what the exact rerun facade is at the nominal run time; a P3 job facade would leave the same question. The fixture composition of the synthetic case set, the owner loads and the case that carries the forced record failure are likewise not fixed.
evidence: Arch v5 extract slide 44 row JOB-03 (owner rwb-case, mechanism DailyCaseRun step); ownership.json jobs JOB-03 replacement 'event-started workflow (DailyCaseRun step in rwb-case)'; ownership.json api GET /admin/jobs owner P1; RWB-E1-020 section 12 restart line 'Rerun from the job monitor'
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-case with the service owner of rwb-source-data
proposed: Publish the JOB-03 step state on the rwb-case run result, keep the catalogue read and the rerun on the P1 job catalogue, and fix the rerun facade for a workflow step in the P1 contract before wave 1 exit.

title: Route-decided transfer trigger has no wave 1 owner event
source: RWB E1 021 Transfer rules and engine v1 v2.md (flow step 1, AC1, BR2); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43 (RouteDecided, rwb-valuation, consumer rwb-case) and slide 42 row 05; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14
description: The legacy TRANSFER row TRF-002 fires on the route-decided fact (rule event ROUTE_APPROVED) carried in CaseStateChanged of the case module. In Arch v5 the route is decided and owned by rwb-valuation (S1), announced as RouteDecided on rwb.valuation.events.v1 to rwb-case, and rwb-valuation is a wave 3 service that a wave 1 integration run cannot observe. The source documents therefore do not fix which event a wave 1 suite must assert for the route-decided trigger, nor whether the fact is committed by rwb-case as CaseStateChanged before or after the S1 announcement.
evidence: Legacy flow step 1: 'CaseStateChanged for a stage change or a route decided (rule event ROUTE_APPROVED)'. Arch v5 slide 43: '+ RouteDecided | rwb-valuation | rwb.valuation.events.v1 | rwb-case'. Arch v5 slide 41 gives S1 wave 3.
proposed: Read the route-decided trigger as the route-decided fact that rwb-case commits as rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1 and assert it there for TRF-002 in wave 1; assert the S1 RouteDecided announcement separately when rwb-valuation lands in wave 3. Recorded as an assumption, no value invented.

title: Claims of the short-lived user JWT and the place of the multi-factor gate are not fixed
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slides 14 and 20); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 022 Sign on with SSO MFA and the first roles v1.md
description: Arch v5 slide 20 gives gateway-bff the ACE common sign-in and a short-lived user JWT, and slide 14 gives rwb-access the ACE common group-to-role call, but no source states which claims the user JWT carries or whether the multi-factor (amr) check is enforced at the edge, in rwb-access or in both. The legacy story puts the check inside the P4 SessionResolver, a single module the target splits between gateway-bff and rwb-access.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 20: 'REST ACE Common sign-in: session -> short-lived user JWT' and 'DB Redis: sessions only; no business data'. Slide 14, rwb-access OUT: 'REST ACE Common: sign-in, group-to-role (Entra)'. Legacy section 4 step 3: 'Workbench (SessionResolver): checks that the amr claim contains mfa'.
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-access; platform owner of gateway-bff
proposed: Fix the claim set of the short-lived user JWT (Entra ID object reference, session ID, amr claim) and enforce the amr mfa check at gateway-bff before any owner call, with rwb-access repeating the check when it resolves the session.

title: RWB-E1-023 integration slice: the S8 deviation read path, the wave of rwb-deviation and the fixture composition are not fixed by the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 023 Case record view v1 read only v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 15, 20, 41); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC18; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Fixtures
description: Three values the run needs are absent or in conflict. (1) The ownership map carries POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} for rwb-deviation but no read of the deviations of a case, while Arch v5 slide 15 names GET /deviations, so the read of AC18 is written as GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations?caseId={caseId} on the S8 base of slide 41. (2) Arch v5 slide 41 puts rwb-deviation in wave 2 and this wave 1 story lists RWB-S8-E1023-APP as an integration dependency, so the service is assumed present in SIT for the run. (3) No source itemises the fixture: the row counts, the document set behind the 50 documents, the 120 ledger entries and the keys of the missing view row are taken as the RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG synthetic set with the keys and values the legacy criteria name.
evidence: ownership.json api keys 'POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations' and 'PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}' with no GET entry for the resource; Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 (rwb-deviation IN: REST GET/POST /deviations) against slide 41 (rwb-deviation, wave 2); WP B-ITG-W1-03 story line RWB-ITG-E1023-ITG I list naming RWB-S8-E1023-APP; RWB-E1-023 section 7 AC12 and AC1 give the 50 documents and the 120 entries but no fixture composition
proposed: Confirm the case-scoped deviation read with the S8 service owner before AC18 is built, treat rwb-deviation as available in SIT for the wave 1 run, and keep the fixture as the W1J01 synthetic set with the values the criteria name
